levels.title_en: ने with तुम, आप and हम

items.pronunciation_notes: तुमने is two syllables with no vowel between म and न: tum-ne.
items.gloss_en: the question you will ask most in this module

learn.title_en: तुमने क्या किया — what did you do
learn.explanation_en: तुम plus ने gives तुमने, and this question is worth over-learning because it is how almost every conversation about the past begins. Note the verb: क्या has no gender of its own, so the verb falls back to the default masculine singular किया. That default will matter again at level thirteen, and for now it is enough to know that when there is nothing for the verb to agree with, it takes the masculine singular.

examples.note: क्या has no gender, so the verb takes the default masculine singular.
The same shape with another transitive verb.
With a real object the verb agrees with it — रोटी is feminine.

common_error.why_en: A pronoun and ने are written as one word. Only noun subjects keep ने separate.

practice.question: तुम + क्या + करना · perfective
practice.explanation_en: तुमने as one word, and किया as the default masculine singular after क्या.

game.explanation_en: तुमने, written as one word. तुम्हें is the को form and does a different job.

items.pronunciation_notes: आपने keeps the long aa of आप: aap-ne.
items.gloss_en: the polite form, and the verb कहना

learn.title_en: आपने, and how to ask someone to repeat themselves
learn.explanation_en: आप plus ने gives आपने, with no surprises — आप has been the easy pronoun since Module 6 and it stays easy here. आपने क्या कहा is what did you say, and it is the polite way to ask someone to repeat themselves. कहना is transitive, so it takes ने. That is worth flagging now because बोलना, which also means to speak, does not — and those two verbs are the subject of level eleven.

examples.note: The polite way to ask someone to repeat something.
कहना is transitive, so ने is needed.
The polite version of the question from the last item.

common_error.why_en: कहना is transitive, so its perfective needs ने however polite the pronoun is.

practice.question: आप + क्या + कहना · perfective
practice.explanation_en: आपने with ने, and कहा as the default masculine singular after क्या.

game.explanation_en: आपने, and the default masculine singular because क्या has no gender.

items.pronunciation_notes: हमने is two syllables with no vowel between म and न: ham-ne.

learn.title_en: हमने, and the subject is still irrelevant
learn.explanation_en: हम plus ने gives हमने. The sentence हमने खाना खाया is worth sitting with, because हम is plural and the verb is singular — खाया, agreeing with खाना. A plural subject and a singular verb in the same short sentence, and both correct. If that still feels wrong, it is the strongest sign that the object-agreement rule has not settled yet, and levels three and four are worth another pass.

examples.note: Plural subject, singular verb — the object decides.
चाय is feminine, so पी.
Here the verb is plural, but because किताबें is — not because हम is.

common_error.why_en: The verb follows खाना, which is singular. Matching it to the plural हम is exactly the instinct to break.

practice.question: हम + चाय + पीना · perfective
practice.explanation_en: चाय is feminine and singular, so पी — whatever the subject is doing.

game.explanation_en: खाना is masculine singular, so खाया — even though हम is plural.

summary.recap_en: तुमने, आपने and हमने all fuse regularly and hold no surprises. हमने खाना खाया is the sentence to test yourself on — a plural subject with a singular verb, because the object is what the verb is looking at.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the third person, and the stems you already know from Module 6.

levels.title_en: ने with यह, वह and तू

items.pronunciation_notes: उसने is built on the stem उस, which you have had since Module 6: us-ne.
items.gloss_en: the third person, on a stem you already know

learn.title_en: उसने is उस plus ने, and उस is not new
learn.explanation_en: Module 6 taught that वह has an oblique stem उस, and that everything attaching to it uses that stem: उसे, उससे, उसका, उसके पास. उसने is the same stem with one more postposition on it. So there is nothing to memorise here — if you can produce उसका, you can produce उसने. The same goes for यह and इस. Seeing ने as just another postposition on a familiar stem removes most of the difficulty.

examples.note: The stem उस, plus ने.
The same stem with का, from Module 6.
बताना takes को for the person told, so मुझे — and ने for the subject.

common_error.why_en: वह has no oblique form of its own — the stem is उस, exactly as with उसे and उसका.

practice.question: वह + कहना · perfective
practice.explanation_en: The oblique stem is उस, so उसने — the same stem as उसका and उसे.

game.explanation_en: ने on the subject, and बताना takes को for the person told.

items.pronunciation_notes: इसने is built on the stem इस, the near counterpart of उस: is-ne.
items.gloss_en: यह becomes इस, exactly as expected

learn.title_en: इसने for this one, उसने for that one
learn.explanation_en: यह gives the stem इस, so इसने. The pair works exactly as इसका and उसका do — इस for something near, उस for something further away, and in practice उसने is far more common because you are usually talking about someone who is not in front of you. इसने tends to appear when pointing at someone present, which can sound blunt, so वह and उसने are the safer default when talking about a person.

examples.note: The stem इस, plus ने.

examples.english: this one gave it to me
examples.note: देना takes को for the recipient, so मुझे.
The distal counterpart, and the one you will use more.

common_error.why_en: यह has the oblique stem इस, exactly as वह has उस. The direct form never takes a postposition.

practice.question: यह + करना · perfective
practice.explanation_en: The oblique stem of यह is इस, so इसने.

game.explanation_en: इसने on the subject, and देना takes को for the recipient.

items.pronunciation_notes: The long uu of तू is kept: tuu-ne.

learn.title_en: तूने completes the set, with the usual warning
learn.explanation_en: तू plus ने gives तूने, and that completes the singular forms. The same warning applies as in Modules 5 and 7: तू is not a neutral option. Between close friends and from parents to small children it is affectionate; to anyone else it is contemptuous. You will meet तूने constantly in film dialogue and song lyrics, so recognise it — but the advice remains not to produce it unless a Hindi speaker has used it on you first.

examples.note: The तू version of the question from level six.
Recognise it; think twice before saying it.
The safe casual form, and the one to use with friends.

common_error.why_en: Not a grammatical error but a social one. With anyone you have just met, तूने is the wrong choice however correct it looks.

practice.prompt_en: Build the perfective form for this pronoun.
practice.question: तू + करना · perfective
practice.explanation_en: तूने. Unusually, तू keeps its direct form before ने rather than using the stem तुझ.

game.question_en: Which form should you use with someone you have just met?
game.explanation_en: आपने is the safe default with anyone you do not already know well.

summary.recap_en: उसने and इसने are built on the oblique stems उस and इस that Module 6 gave you, so nothing about them is new — ने is just one more postposition on a familiar stem. तूने completes the singular set and carries the same register warning as तू itself.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the plural forms, including the one that almost nobody gets right first time.

levels.title_en: The plural forms, and the trap

items.pronunciation_notes: Three syllables with a nasal in the middle: un-hoṁ-ne, not un-ne.

learn.explanation_en: This is the one irregular form in the whole set. वे has the oblique stem उन, which gives उनका, उनसे and उनके पास exactly as expected — and then with ने it becomes उन्होंने rather than the उनने you would predict. There is no reason and no pattern; it simply has an extra syllable. It is also extremely common, because it covers not just they but any single person you are speaking about respectfully. So this is the ने form you will hear most after उसने, and the one worth drilling hardest.

examples.english: they said, or he said politely
examples.note: The irregular form — three syllables, not two.
The regular stem उन with का, for comparison.
The verb still agrees with खाना, not with the subject.

common_error.why_en: उनने is what the pattern predicts and it is not a word. This form has to be memorised on its own.

practice.question: वे + कहना · perfective
practice.explanation_en: उन्होंने — irregular, with a syllable the other forms do not have.

game.explanation_en: उन्होंने, and खाया agreeing with the masculine खाना.

items.pronunciation_notes: The same three-syllable shape as उन्होंने, with the near stem: in-hoṁ-ne.
items.gloss_en: the near plural, irregular in the same way

learn.explanation_en: ये gives the stem इन, and with ने it becomes इन्होंने — irregular in exactly the same way as उन्होंने. So the two plurals behave identically, which at least means there is only one irregularity to remember rather than two. The full set is now complete: मैंने, तूने, तुमने, आपने, हमने, इसने, उसने, इन्होंने, उन्होंने. Seven of the nine are entirely predictable from Module 6; only the last two have to be learnt outright.

examples.note: The near plural, irregular in the same way as उन्होंने.
The regular stem इन with का, for comparison.
बताना takes को for the person told.

common_error.why_en: Like उनने, इनने is what the pattern predicts and is not a word.

game.explanation_en: The two plurals. Everything else follows the Module 6 stems exactly.

items.pronunciation_notes: With a noun subject ने stands apart: lo-goṁ ne.

learn.title_en: Nouns are easier than pronouns here
learn.explanation_en: A noun subject does two simple things and nothing else: it goes oblique, and ने is written as a separate word after it. लोग becomes लोगों, and then लोगों ने. No fusion, no irregularity, no memorisation — just the oblique rule from Module 6 applied as usual. That is worth noticing, because it means the only difficult part of this whole level is the two pronoun forms. Every noun in the language behaves the same predictable way.

examples.note: Oblique plural, and ने written separately.
बच्चा goes to बच्चों before ने.
A Class 2 noun shows no change, but ने is still separate.

common_error.why_en: लोग is plural and ने is a postposition, so the oblique plural लोगों is required.

practice.question: बच्चे + खाना + खाना · perfective
practice.explanation_en: Oblique plural बच्चों, ने written separately, and खाया agreeing with खाना.

game.explanation_en: Oblique plural, and ने as a separate word — only pronouns fuse.

summary.recap_en: The set is complete: मैंने, तूने, तुमने, आपने, हमने, इसने, उसने, इन्होंने, उन्होंने. Only the last two are irregular, and they are irregular in the same way. Noun subjects are entirely predictable — oblique, with ने written separately.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the verbs that take no ने at all, and why they are the easy half of the module.

items.pronunciation_notes: No fusion here — मैं stays as it is: maiṁ ga-yaa.

learn.title_en: With no object, everything goes back to normal
learn.explanation_en: मैं गया is I went, and there is no ने because जाना takes no object. And once ने is absent, the whole sentence reverts to the pattern from Module 7: the subject is plain and the verb agrees with it. So intransitive perfectives are not a new thing to learn at all — they are the ordinary Hindi you already had, and this module simply does not touch them. That is why the intransitive half is the easy half.

examples.note: Said by a man — the verb agrees with the subject, as normal.
Said by a woman, and the verb follows her.
Transitive, so ने appears and the subject stops controlling the verb.

common_error.why_en: जाना takes no object, so no ने. This is the over-application error, and it is as common as forgetting ने in the first place.

practice.question: मैं + जाना · perfective · masculine
practice.explanation_en: जाना is intransitive, so no ने and the verb agrees with the subject.

game.explanation_en: Only खाना, because it takes an object. The other three verbs do not.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two vowels running together with no consonant between: aa-ii.
items.gloss_en: the verb agrees with the subject again

learn.title_en: The subject is back in charge
learn.explanation_en: वह आई is she came, and the verb is feminine because she is. Set that beside उसने रोटी खाई, where the verb is feminine because the roti is, and you have the whole module in two sentences. Same person, same gender of verb ending, two completely different reasons. Which reason applies depends on one thing only: whether the verb takes an object.

examples.note: Feminine because the subject is — the ordinary pattern.
Feminine because the object is. The subject could be anyone.
बैठना is intransitive, so the subject controls the verb.

common_error.why_en: आना takes no object. Adding ने to an intransitive verb is the single most common overcorrection in this module.

practice.question: वह (feminine) + आना · perfective
practice.explanation_en: आना is intransitive, so no ने and the verb agrees with the feminine subject.

game.explanation_en: बैठना is intransitive, so no ने at all.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both words end on a short e: ham bai-ṭhe.
items.gloss_en: a plural subject, and the verb follows it

learn.title_en: हम बैठे against हमने खाना खाया
learn.explanation_en: हम बैठे has a plural verb because हम is plural. हमने खाना खाया, from level six, has a singular verb despite the same plural subject — because there the object is singular and the subject has no say. Putting the two side by side is the clearest test of whether the rule has settled: if you can explain why one verb is plural and the other is not, you have it.

examples.note: Plural verb, agreeing with the plural subject.
Singular verb, agreeing with the singular object.
Intransitive, so the subject controls the verb.

common_error.why_en: बैठना takes no object, so no ने — and then the subject controls the verb as normal.

practice.question: वे + आना · perfective · masculine
practice.explanation_en: आना is intransitive, so no ने and the verb agrees with the plural subject.

game.explanation_en: Only खाना takes an object. The rest are intransitive.

summary.recap_en: Intransitive perfectives are simply Module 7, untouched — no ने, and the verb agrees with the subject. वह आई and उसने रोटी खाई both end in a feminine verb for completely different reasons, and which reason applies depends only on whether the verb takes an object.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the verbs that look transitive and are not, and a conversation that switches between the two in consecutive lines.

levels.title_en: Verbs that look transitive and are not

items.pronunciation_notes: मिली is two light syllables ending long: mi-lii.
items.gloss_en: a person and a thing, and still no ने

learn.title_en: मिलना has a person and a thing and is still intransitive
learn.explanation_en: मुझे किताब मिली is I got the book. There is a person and there is a thing, which makes it look exactly like a transitive sentence — and it is not. मिलना is intransitive, so there is no ने. The trick is to see who is doing what: the book is the subject, it is the thing that arrived, and मुझे is where it arrived. That is why the verb is मिली, agreeing with किताब as any subject would. लगना works the same way, which is why मुझे भूख लगी has no ने either.

examples.note: किताब is the subject, so मिली agrees with it — and no ने.
लगना is intransitive too, and भूख is the subject.
लेना is transitive, so this one does take ने — compare it directly.

common_error.why_en: मिलना is intransitive. The book comes to you, so you take को rather than ने.

practice.question: मैं + किताब + मिलना · perfective
practice.explanation_en: मिलना is intransitive — the person takes को and the thing is the subject.

game.explanation_en: Only लेना, which is transitive. मिलना and लगना are not, despite looking as though they should be.

items.pronunciation_notes: सोया is two syllables with a य between them: so-yaa.
items.gloss_en: the test — can you do it to something?

learn.title_en: The question to ask: can this verb take an object?
learn.explanation_en: When you are unsure, ask whether the verb can take a thing after it. You can eat something, read something, buy something — those are transitive and take ने. You cannot sleep something, go something or sit something — those are intransitive and never do. It is not a perfect test, because a few verbs behave oddly and those are level eleven, but it settles the overwhelming majority. मैं सोया, I slept, with no object anywhere and therefore no ने.

examples.note: You cannot sleep something, so no ने.
Laughing takes no object either.
You see something, so देखना is transitive and takes ने.

common_error.why_en: Sleeping takes no object, so no ने. Apply the test before reaching for it.

practice.question: वह + हँसना · perfective · masculine
practice.explanation_en: हँसना takes no object, so no ने and the verb agrees with the subject.

game.question_en: Which verb can take an object, and so needs ने?
game.explanation_en: देखना — you see something. The other three take no object at all.

items.pronunciation_notes: ख़रीदी has the throaty ख़ and ends on a long ii: kha-rii-dii.
items.gloss_en: the same speaker, with and without ने

learn.title_en: Two lines apart, and the construction switches
learn.explanation_en: The same speaker says मैं बाज़ार गया and then मैंने सब्ज़ी ख़रीदी, two lines apart. Nothing about him changed — the verb did. जाना takes no object so the subject stays plain and the verb agrees with him; ख़रीदना takes one, so ने appears and the verb switches to agreeing with सब्ज़ी instead. That switch, inside a single short exchange, is what this module is for. Note the first line too: तुम कहाँ गए uses plural agreement because तुम always does.

common_error.why_en: जाना is intransitive. बाज़ार is a destination, not an object, so there is nothing for ने to mark.

practice.question: मैं + सब्ज़ी + ख़रीदना · perfective
practice.explanation_en: ने on the subject, and ख़रीदी agreeing with the feminine सब्ज़ी.

game.question_en: Listen to the last line. Which word is missing?
game.explanation_en: सब्ज़ी is feminine and singular, so the verb is ख़रीदी.

summary.recap_en: मिलना and लगना have a person and a thing in the sentence and are still intransitive — the thing is the subject and the person takes को. The working test is whether the verb can take an object at all: you can eat something but you cannot sleep something.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the exceptions — three transitive verbs that refuse ने anyway.
